requirements.title: Each program unit or subprogram has exactly one END statement
requirements.definition: Each program unit, module subprogram, and internal subprogram shall have exactly one END statement.

requirements.title: Executable END statements may be branch targets
requirements.definition: END PROGRAM, END FUNCTION, END SUBROUTINE, and END MP SUBPROGRAM statements are executable and may be branch targets; module, submodule and block-data END statements are not executable.

pending.end-program-branch-target: Compile PROGRAM p with GO TO 100 and labelled 100 END PROGRAM; earlier assignment sets x=99 and no statement after END is used as an oracle.
pending.end-subroutine-branch-target: Compile SUBROUTINE s with GO TO 200 and labelled 200 END SUBROUTINE; caller initializes x=-100, s assigns x=100 before the branch, caller checks x.
pending.nonexecutable-module-end-boundary: Source-control contrasts the executable END SUBROUTINE branch target with an END MODULE label; no runtime branch to END MODULE is planned.

requirements.title: Executing procedure END is equivalent to RETURN with no scalar integer expression
requirements.definition: Executing END FUNCTION, END SUBROUTINE, or END MP SUBPROGRAM is equivalent to executing RETURN with no scalar integer expression.

requirements.title: Module, submodule, and block-data END statements are nonexecutable
requirements.definition: END MODULE, END SUBMODULE, and END BLOCK DATA statements are nonexecutable.
